newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-AIK AND BARCELONA PROMISE TO ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AIK AND BARCELONA PROMISE TO ATTACK.

text.p: AIK Stockholm and Barcelona both promised an attacking display when they meet each other in the European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-finals on Thursday.

The Swedes lost the first leg in Spain 3-1 but manager Stefan Soderberg said his side were psyched up for the return match after thrashing second division Vasalund 7-0 in the Swedish Cup last weekend.
"We have to score at least two goals to win on aggregate, that's simple mathematics," Soderberg said. "This means we have to be aggressive and play attacking football."
"It's a pleasure for us that Swedish soccer fans are able to see one of the best teams in the world live in Sweden and we're going to do our best to give Barcelona a tough match."
Thomas Lagerlof and Cesar Pacha scored two goals each in the defeat of Vasalund while Johan Mjallby, Ola Andersson and Krister Nordin scored the other three.
But Nordin is not eligible for Thursday's match at Rasunda in Stockholm after being sent off at Nou Camp on March 6.
Despite the first leg lead, Barcelona coach Bobby Robson was taking no chances and will play Brazil's World Footballer of the Year Ronaldo -- to the delight of the Swedish media and soccer fans.
"Ronaldo will play because we are going out to score. We will play an attacking game," Robson said. "The tie isn't decided yet."
Robson, who left Spain for Sweden on Tuesday after storming out of a press conference in which he called a reporter "a liar", is in no mood for upsets.
The former England coach has changed his team considerably since their spectacular come-back from 3-0 down to win 5-4 in the Spanish Cup against Atletico Madrid.
Strikers Juan Pizzi and Hristo Stoichkov are likely to be on the bench while midfielder Ivan de la Pena looks likely to take the place of Brazilian international Giovanni.

But Robson will be forced to leave utility player Luis Enrique Martinez, who picked up his second booking of the competition in the first leg, and French defender Laurent Blanc, who was sent off towards the end of the game.
Barcelona's worst enemy may be the intense cold in Stockholm where temperatures are expected to be around zero degrees Celsius for the evening match.
"We'll wear coats and nothing will happen," Barcelona midfielder Guillermo Amor said.
Ronaldo shrugged off questions about the cold when he was met by hordes of reporters and fans on arrival at Stockholm's international airport on Tuesday night -- in minus six degrees Celsius.
"Ronaldo is the world's coolest goal scorer ... and he has never been cooler than he was last night," said Swedish tabloid Expressen.
A spokeswoman for AIK said a final line-up had not been named but all players were available.
Teams (probable):
AIK - Magnus Hedman, Per Millqvist, Mikael Brundin, Johan Mjallby, Gary Sundgren, Nebojsa Novakovic, Ola Andersson, Thomas Lagerlof, Pierre Gallo, Pascal Simpson, Cesar Pacha.
Barcelona - Vitor Baia, Abelardo Fernandez, Miguel Angel Nadal, Albert Ferrer, Sergi Barjuan, Josep Guardiola, Gheorghe Popescu, Ivan de la Pena, Luis Figo, Ronaldo, Luis Figo.
